note: UNTSF-COMM starter catalogue: TSFs, equipment, manufacturers, organisations, rules, settings and the 2012 situation map.

items.label: STANDBY
items.meaning: Available but not assigned to active duty

v1.label: Initial rules
v1.notes: Default 1-100 caps; rating weights from the design spec.

fac-nldc.name: Northern Littoral Defence Command
fac-nldc.description: Original faction: a Scandinavian coalition holding the northern sea lanes.

mfr-mitsubishi.name: Mitsuhishi Heavy Industries
mfr-mitsubishi.description: Japanese TSF maker; jointly develops and builds most Japanese TSFs with Fugaku and Kawazaki (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-fugaku.name: Fugaku Heavy Industries
mfr-fugaku.description: Japanese TSF maker; jointly develops and builds most Japanese TSFs with Mitsuhishi and Kawazaki (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-kawasaki.name: Kawazaki
mfr-kawasaki.description: Japanese TSF maker; co-developer of the Type-77, Type-82, F-15J, Type-94 and Type-97 (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-lockheed.name: Lockweed Mardin
mfr-lockheed.description: In-universe builder of the F-22A, per the Muv-Luv Wiki (a nod to Lockheed Martin).

mfr-boeing.name: Boening
mfr-boeing.description: US maker; took over McDaell Doglam lines after the merger; F-15ACTV and XFJ partner (Muv-Luv Wiki and fan references).

mfr-hks.name: Halvorsen-Kade Systems
mfr-hks.description: Original manufacturer: a Norwegian-Scottish consortium building light scout TSFs.

mfr-mcdaell.name: McDaell Doglam
mfr-mcdaell.description: Builder of the F-4 Phantom and F-15 Eagle; merged into Boening (Muv-Luv Wiki and fan references).

mfr-gendyn.name: General Dynomics
mfr-gendyn.description: F-16 developer; its TSF division was sold to Lockweed in 1993 (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-northrock.name: Northrock
mfr-northrock.description: Competitor in the ATSF programme with the YF-23 (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-sufoni.name: Sufoni
mfr-sufoni.description: Soviet design bureau that developed the Su-27 Zhuravlik (Muv-Luv Wiki).

mfr-mikoyam.name: Mikoyam Guluvich
mfr-mikoyam.description: Soviet design bureau behind the MiG TSFs (fan references; confirm on the wiki).

mfr-panavia.name: Panavia Aircraft
mfr-panavia.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-dassault.name: Dassault Aviation
mfr-dassault.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-eurofighter.name: Eurofighter
mfr-eurofighter.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-shenyang.name: Shenyang Aircraft Corporation
mfr-shenyang.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-chengdu.name: Chengdu Aircraft Industry Group
mfr-chengdu.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-grumman.name: Grumman
mfr-grumman.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mfr-fairchild.name: Fairchild Republic
mfr-fairchild.description: Real-world manufacturer of the aircraft this TSF is named after; no Muv-Luv source found.

mdl-shiranui.name: Shiranui
mdl-shiranui.lore: Japan's first domestically developed third-generation TSF, built for agile close-quarters fighting.

mdl-fubuki.name: Fubuki
mdl-fubuki.lore: Advanced trainer sharing much of the Shiranui design lineage. Forgiving handling, light armament.

mdl-raptor.name: Raptor
mdl-raptor.lore: Stealth-focused third-generation TSF. Export is prohibited; allocation needs GM sign-off.

mdl-strike-eagle.name: Strike Eagle
mdl-strike-eagle.lore: Heavily upgraded Eagle airframe with third-generation avionics. Durable, hard-hitting, less agile.

mdl-varg.name: Varg
mdl-varg.lore: Original design. A light scout frame with an oversized sensor mast and three internal bays.

mdl-f4.name: Phantom
mdl-f4.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. The original TSF: conceived as a walking tank, heavily armoured, and costly in its first deployments.

mdl-f5.name: Freedom Fighter
mdl-f5.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Lighter, more agile first-generation design that marked the shift away from armour.

mdl-tornado.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Late first-generation European TSF built on lessons from the BETA.

mdl-mirage3.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. French late first-generation TSF.

mdl-mig21.name: Balalaika
mdl-mig21.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Soviet F-4 derivative upgraded for close quarters.

mdl-j8.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Chinese first-generation TSF upgraded for close combat.

mdl-type77.name: Gekishin
mdl-type77.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Japanese F-4 derivative with improved close-quarters capability.

mdl-type82.name: Zuikaku
mdl-type82.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Heavily upgraded 1.5th-generation machine, still held back by its first-generation frame.

mdl-f15.name: Eagle
mdl-f15.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. The heavy half of the High-Low Mix.

mdl-f15j.name: Kagerou
mdl-f15j.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Acquired by Japan as a stopgap during its own TSF programme’s difficulties.

mdl-su27.name: Zhuravlik
mdl-su27.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Soviet heavy second-generation TSF of the High-Low Mix.

mdl-f16.name: Fighting Falcon
mdl-f16.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. The lightweight half of the High-Low Mix.

mdl-mig27.name: Aligatori
mdl-mig27.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Soviet lightweight second-generation TSF.

mdl-mig23.name: Cheburashka
mdl-mig23.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Quasi-second-generation Soviet TSF.

mdl-mig25.name: Spirt-Voz
mdl-mig25.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. A poorly developed Soviet second-generation design.

mdl-f18ef.name: Super Hornet
mdl-f18ef.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. 2.5th-generation upgrade built on proven second-generation technology.

mdl-f15actv.name: Active Eagle
mdl-f15actv.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Second-generation airframe partly upgraded with third-generation technology.

mdl-f15se.name: Silent Eagle
mdl-f15se.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Quasi-third-generation Eagle that may be reclassified as full third generation.

mdl-mig29ovt.name: Fulcrum
mdl-mig29ovt.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Quasi-third-generation Soviet upgrade.

mdl-type00.name: Takemikazuchi
mdl-type00.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Late third-generation TSF built for overwhelming close-combat advantage.

mdl-su37m2.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Soviet third-generation close-combat TSF.

mdl-j10x.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Chinese third-generation TSF, fielded with Type-77 Battle Halberds.

mdl-ef2000.name: Typhoon
mdl-ef2000.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. European third-generation TSF combining mobility with heavy firepower.

mdl-a6.name: Intruder
mdl-a6.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Tactical Surface Attacker: massive firepower and armour, little speed.

mdl-a10.name: Thunderbolt II
mdl-a10.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Tactical Surface Attacker built to stop BETA advances head-on.

mdl-a12.name: Avenger
mdl-a12.lore: From the Muv-Luv Wiki TSF overview. Tactical Surface Attacker for clearing operations and beachheads.

eq-type87.name: Type-87 Assault Cannon
eq-type87.description: Standard Japanese assault cannon: 36mm main gun with a 120mm under-barrel launcher.

eq-ws16c.name: WS-16C Assault Cannon
eq-ws16c.description: Widely issued western assault cannon. Reliable and easy to resupply.

eq-amws21.name: AMWS-21 Combat System
eq-amws21.description: Dedicated rifle system developed alongside the F-22A.

eq-hkr2.name: HK-R2 Carbine
eq-hkr2.description: Original design. Compact carbine for scout frames; trades punch for handling.

eq-type74.name: Type-74 PB Long Blade
eq-type74.description: Two-handed close-combat long sword, carried on a mount arm.

eq-type65.name: Type-65 Close Combat Knife
eq-type65.description: Forearm-stowed combat knife for grappling range.

eq-mmc4.name: MMC-4 Missile Container
eq-mmc4.description: Original design. Mount-arm missile container for saturation strikes.

eq-hk90.name: HK-90 Support Cannon
eq-hk90.description: Original design. Long-barrelled support cannon for overwatch.

eq-sensor-array.name: Enhanced Sensor Array
eq-sensor-array.description: Original design. Wide-angle sensor package that feeds the pilot a better picture.

eq-mirage3.name: Mirage-3 ECM Pod
eq-mirage3.description: Original design. Experimental jamming pod. Field trials only.

eq-jump-kit.name: High-Output Jump Unit Kit
eq-jump-kit.description: Original design. Uprated jump unit nozzles and fuel management.

eq-hk-frame.name: Halvorsen-Kade Lightweight Frame
eq-hk-frame.description: Original design. Lightened structural members for HK airframes.

eq-link-node.name: Formation Link Node
eq-link-node.description: Original design. Prototype squad data-link for flight leads.

eq-em-lance.name: Electromagnetic Lance Prototype
eq-em-lance.description: Original design. One-off rail weapon. Issued by the GM for specific operations.

eq-ju108.name: JU-108 Jump Unit
eq-ju108.description: Original design. Standard jet/rocket hybrid jump unit for third-generation frames. Factory fit on most Japanese TSFs.

eq-ju90t.name: JU-90T Training Jump Unit
eq-ju90t.description: Original design. Detuned jump unit with conservative rocket limits for trainee pilots.

eq-ju120w.name: JU-120W Jump Unit
eq-ju120w.description: Original design. Heavy western jump unit sized for strike airframes.

compat.reason: RESTRICTED: Built only for the F-22A.

eq-ju150s.name: JU-150S Low-Observable Jump Unit
eq-ju150s.description: Original design. High-thrust jump unit with shielded exhausts, built only for the F-22A.

eq-ju132.name: JU-132 High-Output Jump Unit
eq-ju132.description: Original design. Uprated turbines and a larger rocket reserve, at the cost of airframe stress.

eq-pdj1.name: PDJ-1 Pulse-Detonation Jump Unit
eq-pdj1.description: Original design. Experimental pulse-detonation unit. Enormous thrust, brutal on the airframe and the pilot.

eq-at12.name: AT-12 Auxiliary Thruster Set
eq-at12.description: Original design. Standard attitude-control thrusters for shoulders, back and legs.

eq-at20.name: AT-20 Vectored Thruster Pack
eq-at20.description: Original design. Vectored nozzles for sharper direction changes in close quarters.

eq-fc3.name: FC-3 Fuel Cell Stack
eq-fc3.description: Original design. Standard fuel cell power plant driving actuators and avionics.

eq-fc5.name: FC-5 Extended Fuel Cell
eq-fc5.description: Original design. Larger stack for long patrols; the extra mass costs agility.

eq-hb2.name: HB-2 High-Density Battery
eq-hb2.description: Original design. Light, high-output battery pack. Short endurance; best for interception sorties.

eq-arm-std.name: Standard Composite Armour
eq-arm-std.description: Anti-projectile, heat-resistant composite with anti-laser coating. Factory armour on every model.

eq-arm-alc.name: Reinforced Anti-Laser Coating
eq-arm-alc.description: Original design. Thicker ablative coating. Buys seconds against Laser-class fire at a weight cost.

eq-arm-light.name: Lightweight Armour Set
eq-arm-light.description: Original design. Strips plating for agility, in line with avoid-don’t-absorb doctrine.

eq-arm-reactive.name: Reactive Armour Plates
eq-arm-reactive.description: Original design. Reactive plates on the shoulders and forearms, after Soviet close-combat practice.

eq-act-std.name: Standard Carbon Actuators
eq-act-std.description: Superconducting carbon bands that contract under current. Factory actuators on every model.

eq-act-hr.name: High-Response Carbon Actuators
eq-act-hr.description: Original design. Faster bands and finer control loops; joints wear sooner.

eq-act-joint.name: Reinforced Joint Set
eq-act-joint.description: Original design. Heavier multi-segment joints that absorb shock on rough ground.

eq-os-std.name: Standard Combat OS
eq-os-std.description: Keeps the actively unstable frame upright and runs motion control. Factory OS on every model.

eq-os-xm3.name: XM3 Operating System
eq-os-xm3.description: Next-generation TSF operating system with input buffering and motion cancelling. Trials only.

eq-fuel-std.name: Internal Leg Tanks
eq-fuel-std.description: Jet fuel for the jump units, carried in the jump units and leg tanks. Factory fit.

eq-fuel-ext.name: External Fuel Tanks
eq-fuel-ext.description: Drop tanks for longer range and operating time. Jettisoned before contact in most doctrines.

eq-fuel-leg.name: Extended Leg Tanks
eq-fuel-leg.description: Original design. Enlarged internal leg tanks.

eq-ju80.name: JU-80 Early Jump Unit
eq-ju80.description: Original design. First-generation jump unit: thirsty, slow to spool, limited rocket reserve.

eq-ju140h.name: JU-140H Heavy Jump Unit
eq-ju140h.description: Original design. High-thrust, low-agility unit for Tactical Surface Attackers.

eq-halberd77.name: Type-77 Battle Halberd
eq-halberd77.description: Long-hafted close-combat weapon carried by Unified Front of China units such as the J-10X.

weapon.special: Reach: strikes before most melee weapons

eq-eac36.name: EAC-36 Assault Cannon
eq-eac36.description: Original design. Rugged eastern-pattern 36 mm assault cannon, built to survive irregular resupply.

weapon.special: Ignores jams from dust and cold

eq-eur36.name: EUR-36 Assault Cannon
eq-eur36.description: Original design. European-pattern assault cannon tuned for suppression fire.

eq-motorblade.name: Forearm Motor Blade
eq-motorblade.description: Original design. Built-in forearm blade in the Soviet close-combat tradition.

weapon.special: Usable while grappled; no hand needed

zone-h1.name: Kashgar Hive (H1)
zone-h1.description: The Original Hive. Destroyed in Operation Ouka, January 2002; its ruins are still watched.

zone-h5.name: Minsk Hive (H5)
zone-h5.description: The hive that broke Operation Palaiologos.

zone-h9.name: Ankara Hive (H9)
zone-h9.description: Threatens the Bosporus and the Levant.

zone-h16.name: Chongqing Hive (H16)
zone-h16.description: The source of the 1998 invasion of Japan.

zone-h20.name: Cheorwon Hive (H20)
zone-h20.description: The last hive within reach of Japan. Priority target.

zone-h21.name: Sadogashima Hive (H21)
zone-h21.description: Destroyed in Operation 21st, December 2001. Sado Island is a restricted zone.

zone-yokohama.name: Yokohama Base
zone-yokohama.description: UN 11th Army, built on the site of the Yokohama Hive (H22), taken in Operation Lucifer, 1999.

zone-sendai.name: Sendai
zone-sendai.description: Imperial capital and Imperial Japanese Army headquarters.

zone-kure.name: Kure
zone-kure.description: Inland Sea base supporting the Sea of Japan coast.

zone-petropavlovsk.name: Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky
zone-petropavlovsk.description: Soviet Far East headquarters behind the Kamchatka line.

zone-ismailia.name: Ismailia
zone-ismailia.description: Headquarters of the Suez Canal defence.

zone-darwin.name: Darwin
zone-darwin.description: Rear base and training area for Asian and Pacific forces.

zone-edwards.name: Edwards
zone-edwards.description: US TSF test and evaluation centre.

zone-northcape.name: Norwegian Sea Patrol
zone-northcape.description: Watches the Arctic flank of occupied Scandinavia.

zone-seaofjapan.name: Sea of Japan Patrol
zone-seaofjapan.description: Coastal watch since Sado fell; BETA crossings from Korea still possible.

zone-tsushima.name: Tsushima Strait Patrol
zone-tsushima.description: Under laser coverage from the Korean coast.

zone-cheorwon.name: Cheorwon Front
zone-cheorwon.description: Allied pressure on H20 from the southern coast.

zone-niigata.name: Sea of Japan Coast
zone-niigata.description: The old Niigata defence line, quieter since Sado fell.

zone-lapland.name: Norwegian Coast
zone-lapland.description: Raids from Shetland on the occupied Norwegian coast.

zone-calais.name: Channel Coast
zone-calais.description: Raids and counter-landings on the French coast.

zone-london.name: London
zone-london.description: European Union government in exile and allied European command.

zone-portsmouth.name: Portsmouth
zone-portsmouth.description: Channel fleet base; landing craft and TSF carriers.

zone-shetland.name: Shetland Forward Base
zone-shetland.description: Forward base for raids on the Norwegian coast.

zone-greenland.name: Narsarsuaq
zone-greenland.description: Greenland station watching for a crossing from Khatanga.

zone-cagliari.name: Cagliari (Sardinia)
zone-cagliari.description: Island outpost off occupied Italy; held by Italian forces in exile.

zone-biscay.name: Bay of Biscay Patrol
zone-biscay.description: Watches the occupied French and Spanish coasts.

zone-cotentin.name: Cotentin Raids
zone-cotentin.description: Raiding operations on the Normandy coast.

zone-rhinedelta.name: Rhine Delta
zone-rhinedelta.description: BETA massing on the Dutch coast opposite East Anglia.

zone-rabat.name: Rabat
zone-rabat.description: African Union western command; European units based in exile.

zone-cairo.name: Cairo
zone-cairo.description: African Union headquarters for the northern fronts.

zone-eastmed.name: Eastern Mediterranean Patrol
zone-eastmed.description: Watches for crossings from occupied Greece and the Levant.

zone-gibraltar.name: Strait of Gibraltar Front
zone-gibraltar.description: The narrowest crossing to Africa. BETA attempt seabed crossings from occupied Spain.

front-eurasia.name: BETA-controlled territory, 2012
front-eurasia.description: Continental Europe is occupied except the British Isles (canon, 2001). Follows national borders; Kamchatka, Chukotka and Sakhalin are held by the Soviet Union. Extrapolated to 2012 from the situation after Operation Ouka.

front-japan.name: Sea of Japan front
front-japan.description: Quieter since Sado fell; Cheorwon (H20) remains.

front-asia.name: South China Sea and Indochina front

front-maghreb.name: Mediterranean front (North Africa)
front-maghreb.description: The African Union’s line along the southern Mediterranean shore.
